title: Unit
description: The atomic thing a person performs and records a separate result for. status: outline relaxes every depth field and nothing else -- an outline still needs a falsifiable objective, because that is the entire content of the file and the whole of what breadth buys.

requires.description: What must already be true for this unit to be possible at all -- not what makes it likely to succeed. Over-declaring here hides tests from the reader who has not yet earned the fact, which is worse than a unit offered slightly too early.

motivated_by.description: Facts that make this unit worth reaching for sooner, without being conditions of it. Kept separate from requires so that a hint can never silently become a gate.

yields.description: What becomes true when the result is positive. This, with requires, is the whole of the chain: no unit names another unit.

closes.description: What a negative result rules out. A subset of yields: a unit can only close a claim it was capable of opening.

allOf.description: kind: test carries an oracle and a completion criterion once authored. Absent kind means test, so nothing written before the field changes meaning.

A recon unit establishes a fact rather than judging the target, so it cannot state an oracle. Forbidding the field is the point: while it was merely optional, units wrote 'not applicable' into it and the field stopped meaning anything.
An inquiry unit is target-specific by nature; it carries questions to ask of the workflow rather than an oracle or a fixed sequence.
done_when is required of every authored unit regardless of kind: 'did I finish this' is a question recon and inquiry units answer as much as any other.
